chunks: Al-Saffar from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'id said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who was killed while he had a debt and left no wealth, so his family took the blood money (diyah) from his killer. Is it upon them to settle the debt? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And he left nothing?' He said, 'They only took the blood money, so it is upon them to settle the debt on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the debt of a deceased person who left no wealth but received blood money?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the receipt of blood money (diyah) by the heirs creates a specific financial liability, obligating them to settle the deceased's debts from these proceeds even if no other assets remain. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that diyah is treated as part of the estate's assets for the purpose of debt repayment, ensuring creditors' rights are preserved before the distribution of inheritance. This highlights the prioritization of financial obligations over the heirs' immediate possession of the compensation.
